assembly_instructions: 1. Bolt the base_frame to the floor at y=0 and mount base_rail_port, base_rail_starboard, post_front_port, post_rear_port, post_front_starboard, and post_rear_starboard to create an open service frame. 2. Install input_plate on the base_frame, then place embedding_table directly above it and connect the residual_pipe through the center of the frame. 3. Attach layer_tray_01 through layer_tray_06 and the two final-layer trays to the posts, leaving gaps between trays so the residual stream is visible. 4. Mount the attention lane on the port side of layer_tray_03 in this order: attn_pre_norm, q_head_fan, kv_head_four_pack, qk_norm_ring, rope_ring, flash_attention_core, and attn_o_proj, then connect the kv_cache_tower to the attention core with kv_cache_bus. 5. Mount the MoE lane on the starboard side of layer_tray_03 in this order: ffn_pre_norm, router_disk, dispatch_bus, active_expert_01 through active_expert_08, grouped_gemm_plate, combine_bus, and moe_output_join. 6. Place dormant_expert_bank_a through dormant_expert_bank_d behind the active experts to show the unused routed capacity of the 128-expert bank. 7. Mount dca_local_chunk, dca_global_chunk, yarn_rescale_ring, mode_selector_think, and mode_selector_no_think above the final layers, then connect them to the attention lane and residual_pipe. 8. Install prediction_head, lm_loss_marker, and output_tokens_plate at the top of the residual path. 9. Attach optimizer_adamw, training_data_pipe, post_train_pipeline, and parallelism_marker to side rails so training and deployment infrastructure is grounded and not floating. 10. Verify every module has a visible connection back to base_frame through either a rail, post, tray, bus, or the residual_pipe.

info.summary: 235B-parameter MoE LM from Alibaba's Qwen team (22B activated per token). 94 layers × 4096 hidden dim, GQA at extreme 64-Q / 4-KV (ratio 16) for tiny KV footprint, 128 fine-grained routed experts (top-8) with NO shared expert, QK-Norm + RoPE on attention, and a hybrid /think + /no_think mode that shares weights. 32K native context extended to 128K with Dual-Chunk Attention + YaRN. Pre-trained on 36T tokens across 119 languages.
info.description:
Qwen3-235B-A22B is the flagship of the Qwen3 family. Compared with Qwen2.5 it (i) goes MoE (was dense at the top size), (ii) drops the shared expert (Qwen2.5-MoE had one) — every active param now comes from learned routing, (iii) introduces hybrid thinking modes /think and /no_think over a single set of weights, (iv) uses QK-Norm + RoPE rather than the QKV-bias quirks of earlier Qwens, (v) extends to 128K context with Dual-Chunk Attention overlapping YaRN. The MoE uses 128 fine-grained experts at top-8 (similar density to DeepSeek-V3's 256-top-8 but at smaller total scale) with the auxiliary-loss-free balancing trick. Routing is softmax with a small balance bias.

Design rationale, in one line each:
• 16:1 GQA: brutally small KV cache; 4 KV heads is the most aggressive in the open-MoE class.
• 128 fine-grained experts no-shared: removes the always-on FFN cost; routing must carry all capacity.
• Hybrid /think /no_think: one model serves both fast chat and deep reasoning by system-tag.
• Dual-Chunk Attention + YaRN: cheap context extension from 32K → 128K without re-pretraining.
• 36 T multilingual corpus, 119 languages: positions Qwen3 as the most multilingual open MoE.

comparisons.delta: Qwen2.5-72B was a dense decoder with QKV bias, GQA at 8 KV heads, no MoE. Qwen3-235B-A22B replaces the dense FFN with 128-expert top-8 MoE (no shared), drops QKV bias, replaces RoPE-only attention with QK-Norm + RoPE, pushes GQA to 16:1, adds hybrid /think /no_think modes, and extends context 32K → 128K via DCA + YaRN. Same tokeniser (151K).

Qwen2-MoE used a SHARED expert plus 64 routed experts at top-8. Qwen3 keeps the fine-grained pattern but DROPS the shared expert and DOUBLES the routed-expert count to 128 — same total active FFN cost but more capacity. Routing changed from sigmoid + aux-loss to softmax + loss-free balance bias.

Both are auxiliary-loss-free fine-grained MoE. V3 has 256 experts top-8 + 1 shared, MLA attention, 671B total; Qwen3-235B-A22B has 128 experts top-8 + NO shared, GQA(64/4), 235B total. V3 has the bigger total capacity and MLA's compressed cache; Qwen3 has aggressive 16:1 GQA so its KV-per-token is actually competitive and its routing footprint is smaller. Qwen3 adds hybrid thinking modes which V3 lacks (DeepSeek-R1 is a separate model).

Versus closed peers, Qwen3 is the most multilingual open MoE (119 languages) and natively supports hybrid /think + /no_think over shared weights — closed peers typically maintain separate fast and reasoning models. Per-token activated is much smaller (22B vs estimated 100B+), trading per-step quality for cost. KV cache at 16:1 GQA is dramatically smaller than full-MHA peers.

parts.name: Open Base Frame
parts.role: The floor plate roots the scene and carries the token input, residual tower, side modules, and service rails.

parts.name: Port Service Rail
parts.role: The port rail carries the attention lane, KV-cache tower, and two left posts.

parts.name: Starboard Service Rail
parts.role: The starboard rail carries the MoE lane, expert bank, mode selector, and deployment panels.

parts.name: Front Port Post
parts.role: This upright post supports the front-left corners of all visible transformer trays.

parts.name: Rear Port Post
parts.role: This upright post supports the rear-left corners of the open transformer ladder.

parts.name: Front Starboard Post
parts.role: This upright post supports the front-right corners of all visible transformer trays.

parts.name: Rear Starboard Post
parts.role: This upright post supports the rear-right corners and keeps the MoE lane visually grounded.

parts.name: Input Tokens: 151,936 Vocab
parts.role: This grounded plate represents the multilingual token-ID stream before embedding lookup.

parts.name: Tied Embedding Table
parts.role: The tied embedding maps each input token into the 4096-channel residual stream.
parts.memory_footprint: 151,936 x 4096 x BF16 is about 1.24 GiB.

parts.name: Residual Stream: d=4096
parts.role: The central vertical pipe carries the 4096-wide residual state through all 94 decoder layers.

parts.name: 94-Layer Count Spine
parts.role: The etched vertical marker states that the eight visible trays stand in for 94 total transformer layers.

parts.name: Transformer Tray 1
parts.role: This open tray represents decoder layer 1 with space for attention on port and MoE on starboard.

parts.name: Transformer Tray 2
parts.role: This open tray represents decoder layer 2 and leaves vertical gaps so the residual pipe is visible.

parts.name: Exploded Transformer Tray 3
parts.role: This cutaway tray exposes one complete layer with the GQA attention lane and routed-MoE FFN lane pulled apart.

parts.name: Transformer Tray 4
parts.role: This open tray represents decoder layer 4 and continues the alternating residual ladder.

parts.name: Transformer Tray 5
parts.role: This open tray represents decoder layer 5 and shows that layers are stacked, not hidden in one block.

parts.name: Transformer Tray 6
parts.role: This open tray represents decoder layer 6 before the skipped middle-layer span.

parts.name: Layers 7-92 Compressed Span
parts.role: This narrow bracket marks the omitted middle 86 layers without hiding the residual pipe.

parts.name: Transformer Tray 93
parts.role: This open tray represents decoder layer 93 after the compressed middle span.

parts.name: Transformer Tray 94 Final
parts.role: This final open tray feeds the tied LM head at the top of the residual path.

parts.name: Attention Pre-RMSNorm
parts.role: This plate normalizes the residual state before QKV projection in the attention sublayer.

parts.name: 64 Query-Head Fan
parts.role: This wide fan represents 64 query heads of dimension 128 before grouped attention.
parts.flops_per_token: Q projection is 2 x 4096 x 64 x 128 multiply-add work per token.

parts.name: 4 KV-Head Pack
parts.role: This compact pack shows that only four KV heads serve all 64 query heads at a 16:1 sharing ratio.
parts.memory_footprint: The per-layer KV projection has only 8 KV-related heads of 128 channels across K and V.

parts.name: QK-Norm Ring
parts.role: This ring applies RMSNorm to Q and K before the dot product for long-context stability.

parts.name: RoPE Ring Base 1,000,000
parts.role: This ring applies rotary positions with a large base used for the extended context path.

parts.name: GQA FlashAttention Core
parts.role: This kernel computes causal GQA attention and accepts DCA chunked attention above 32K context.
parts.flops_per_token: At 32K context the attention term is about 2 x 64 x 128 x 32768 operations per token.
parts.algorithm: if T <= 32768 use flash attention; otherwise combine local chunks and DCA global chunks with YaRN-rescaled RoPE.

parts.name: Attention O-Projection
parts.role: This projection returns the attended state to the 4096-channel residual stream.

parts.name: Paged KV Cache Tower
parts.role: This vertical store holds paged K and V tensors for all layers using only four KV heads.
parts.memory_footprint: About 2 x 4 x 128 x FP8 per token per layer, or roughly 12 GiB for 94 layers at 128K.

parts.name: KV Cache Bus
parts.role: This horizontal bus connects the compact four-head KV cache to the attention core.

parts.name: MoE FFN Pre-RMSNorm
parts.role: This plate normalizes the residual state before the routed MoE feed-forward layer.

parts.name: Top-8 Softmax Router
parts.role: This disk scores 128 experts and chooses the top eight without a shared expert path.
parts.flops_per_token: Router projection is about 2 x 4096 x 128 operations per token.
parts.memory_footprint: Router weight is 4096 x 128 BF16, about 1 MiB per layer.
parts.algorithm: scores = softmax(x @ W_router) + balance_bias; topk_idx, topk_w = topk(scores, 8).

parts.name: Expert Dispatch Bus
parts.role: This bus sends token groups from the router to the eight selected experts.

parts.name: Active Expert 1 of Top-8
parts.role: This selected SwiGLU expert processes its routed token shard with d_ff=1536.

parts.name: Active Expert 2 of Top-8
parts.role: This selected SwiGLU expert processes a second routed token shard with the same fine-grained width.

parts.name: Active Expert 3 of Top-8
parts.role: This selected SwiGLU expert is one of eight activated experts for the current token.

parts.name: Active Expert 4 of Top-8
parts.role: This selected SwiGLU expert contributes a weighted FFN output to the combine step.

parts.name: Active Expert 5 of Top-8
parts.role: This selected SwiGLU expert shows the second row of the top-8 activation set.

parts.name: Active Expert 6 of Top-8
parts.role: This selected SwiGLU expert is routed by learned softmax weights rather than a fixed shared expert.

parts.name: Active Expert 7 of Top-8
parts.role: This selected SwiGLU expert makes the top-8 route visible as separate hardware.

parts.name: Active Expert 8 of Top-8
parts.role: This selected SwiGLU expert completes the eight active experts used per token.

parts.name: Dormant Expert Bank 1-32
parts.role: This compact plate represents routed experts 1-32 when they are not selected for the current token.

parts.name: Dormant Expert Bank 33-64
parts.role: This compact plate represents routed experts 33-64 that remain resident but inactive for this token.

parts.name: Dormant Expert Bank 65-96
parts.role: This compact plate represents routed experts 65-96 and shows the inactive capacity behind top-8 routing.

parts.name: Dormant Expert Bank 97-128
parts.role: This compact plate completes the 128-expert routed bank and confirms that there is no shared expert.

parts.name: Grouped GEMM Plate
parts.role: This plate fuses the eight selected expert matrix multiplications into grouped GEMM launches.
parts.flops_per_token: Eight experts each perform roughly 3 x 2 x 4096 x 1536 operations before weighting.
parts.algorithm: For each routed group, compute SwiGLU gate, up, and down projections, then weight by router probability.

parts.name: Expert Combine Bus
parts.role: This bus gathers weighted expert outputs before returning them to the residual stream.

parts.name: MoE Residual Join
parts.role: This join adds the routed FFN output back into the central residual stream.

parts.name: Expert All-to-All Ring
parts.role: This ring represents NCCL dispatch and combine traffic across expert-parallel ranks.

parts.name: DCA Local 32K Chunk
parts.role: This upper module keeps the trained 32K local attention window intact during long-context inference.

parts.name: DCA Global Chunk Stitcher
parts.role: This module stitches multiple 32K chunks into a 128K context path without re-pretraining.

parts.name: YaRN RoPE Rescale Ring
parts.role: This ring rescales RoPE frequencies so the 32K-trained attention can operate at 128K.

parts.name: Mode Selector: /think
parts.role: This selector routes the same weights through a larger reasoning decode budget when /think is present.
parts.algorithm: If the system prompt contains /think, use the reasoning template and a larger decode budget.

parts.name: Mode Selector: /no_think
parts.role: This selector routes the same weights through a shorter direct-answer decode budget when /no_think is present.

parts.name: Tied LM Head
parts.role: This tied projection converts the final residual state back to logits over the 151,936-token vocabulary.
parts.flops_per_token: Final logits cost about 2 x 4096 x 151,936 operations per token.

parts.name: Cross-Entropy Loss Marker
parts.role: This marker represents next-token loss during pre-training and reward objectives during post-training.

parts.name: Output Token Plate
parts.role: This plate is the decoded token stream produced after sampling from the LM head logits.

parts.name: 36T-Token Multilingual Corpus
parts.role: This grounded feeder represents about 36 trillion training tokens across 119 languages.

parts.name: AdamW Optimizer Cabinet
parts.role: This cabinet represents AdamW state and update logic for the 235B-parameter training run.
parts.memory_footprint: Adam moment state is about two extra parameter copies before sharding.

parts.name: SFT and RL Post-Training Stack
parts.role: This stack represents supervised instruction tuning, preference optimization, and reasoning reinforcement learning after pre-training.

parts.name: TP x EP x PP x DP Panel
parts.role: This side panel documents tensor, expert, pipeline, and data parallelism as the build plan for training and inference.
